correctness.rationale: After at least one positive answer, the excluded vertices form either the empty set or one contiguous subinterval of one gap. A positive query splits the gap; a negative query pins an excluded block, whose two endpoint choices are independent threshold classes of sizes a and L-a. Balanced threshold trees and cardinality give their individual ranks; concatenation and induction on the queried factor give additivity. The two first-query branches are complementary, and no split remains for a singleton (including the n=1 boundary after the first query). This proves the exact recurrence and partition state bound. A fresh calculation evaluated it through 40, reproducing all ten thresholds. Direct explicit-concept minimax through six gave ranks 1,2,3,3,4,4 and class sizes 2,4,8,14,22,32. All 16 paths of the frozen six-vertex witness realize distinct valid concepts. The balance obstruction also checks: after query 0 with answer positive, reflection swaps the two balanced choices 2 and 4, so one can take 2. After its positive branch only 4 balances, and after its positive branch no query balances. The source's wording about reflection is imprecise but does not change the argument. Replay: branches/85039b4a-708f-4e3f-8be7-3b9f8ce330b2/independent_cyclic_arc_check.py and INDEPENDENT_CHECK.txt. The through-40 check used the proved gap recurrence; the independent explicit-concept method was used only through six. No uploaded code was executed. Alternating labels on four points and realizability on three give the VC assertion, and the two equally spaced marked points give the stated asymptotic by the threshold product.

At such a node there is a surviving ordinary nonempty interval, and querying any point it contains separates it from the dummy singleton instead. Thus deleting the dummy query does not lower the attainable depth.
